findings.title: Conditional passkey UI is no longer rendered on the initial login page (no user set)
findings.body: The block that calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is now guarded by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()). That helper returns false when user == null (`... && user != null`). On the normal first-step login, where no user is in the context, the guard is false, so the WebAuthn conditional UI data is never filled. The previous code filled it exactly in that case (`if (webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled())` inside the no-user branch). Result: discoverable passkeys stop appearing in the username/password login page, which is the main passkey login path, and the existing tests that expect the 'username webauthn' autocomplete and the webauth form on the first page would fail.

findings.title: Error challenge drops passkey data when no user has been identified yet
findings.body: challenge(context, error, field) now only calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true, which requires a non-null user. Previously the call was made when the user was null (the conditional UI case). So when the username/password form is re-rendered with an error before any user is identified, the passkey (conditional UI) setup is lost and the page no longer offers passkey login.

findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not match the declared method
findings.body: In UsernamePasswordForm the only declaration added is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which takes one argument. Here it is called as `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no argument. Unless another no-arg overload exists (none is shown in the diff), this does not compile, so the services module would fail to build.

findings.title: configureTestRealm(...) is called but not defined in this class
findings.body: addTestRealms calls configureTestRealm(realmRepresentation). The method is not declared in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, and the diff does not add it. If it is not inherited from AbstractWebAuthnVirtualTest, the test class will not compile. Even if it is inherited, the reviewer needs to confirm which realm changes it applies, since the diff does not show them.

findings.title: Constant widened from protected to public without need
findings.body: USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is changed from protected to public so AuthenticatorUtils (in another package) can import it. This exposes an internal authenticator note key as public API of an exported class. A public accessor or moving the constant to a shared util class would avoid expanding the public surface of AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.

findings.title: NoSuchElementException import is left unused after the assertion change
findings.body: After replacing the two Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) checks with findElement assertions, the NoSuchElementException import on line 51 is no longer referenced in this file. This will produce an unused import warning and may fail a checkstyle or lint build.

findings.title: PR description is only a placeholder
findings.body: The description reads only 'Test 1'. It does not explain the bug being fixed (passkey re-authentication with prompt=login), the approach, or the behaviour change to the conditional UI for users who are not yet identified. A maintainer reviewing this change would need that context, especially given the regression risk in the conditional UI logic.
